item.title: A Drone Killed Three Ukrainians. It Was Guided Entirely by A.I.
item.description: An attack by what Ukrainian officials said was a Russian drone with an Nvidia chip presages a dystopian future of weaponry untethered to humans.
item.dc:creator: Andrew E. Kramer and Nicole Tung
item.media:credit: Nicole Tung for The New York Times

item.title: Some of Russia’s A.I. Drones Are Powered by Nvidia Microcomputers, Ukrainian Officials Say
item.description: The tech giant says it does not sell the devices in Russia, but they are widely available on resale markets. When purchased that way, they are virtually impossible to track.
item.dc:creator: Andrew E. Kramer
item.media:credit: Nicole Tung for The New York Times
item.media:description: A Nvidia Jetson Orin minicomputer that Ukrainian officials say was found in an autonomous drone that Russia recently tested in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine.

item.title: UK Prime Minister Burnham Arrives in Ukraine as Russia Amps Up Warnings
item.description: In his first foreign trip since taking office, Prime Minister Andy Burnham affirmed support for Kyiv despite new warnings from Moscow of potential consequences.
item.dc:creator: Michael D. Shear
item.media:credit: Pool photo by Henry Nicholls
item.media:description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham of Britain on Monday at the tomb of the unknown soldier at Ukraine’s national military memorial cemetery in Hatne, southwest of Kyiv.

item.title: U.S. to Unveil ‘Economic D-Day’ Sanctions Targeting Iran’s Economy
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will hold a news conference outlining the new package of measures.
item.dc:creator: Alan Rappeport
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Kenny Holston/The New York Times
item.media:description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said last week that countries that continue to do business with Iran would face the “full might and force” of the U.S. government.

item.title: Iran Cracks Down on One Luxury Left to Its Youth: Coffee Shops
item.description: In recent weeks, the police have closed dozens of cafes, often citing laws that stipulate women must veil in public. Experts say the closures are part of an effort to control public space.
item.dc:creator: Leily Nikounazar and Yeganeh Torbati
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Arash Khamooshi/Polaris for The New York Times
item.media:description: Iranians at a cafe in Tehran in April.

item.title: Iran Pledges to Defy Trump’s Economic Sanctions
item.description: Analysts say Tehran could intensify the dispute militarily after attempts to squeeze its economy. An Iranian official vowed “not a single drop of oil” would leave the Gulf.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Boxerman and Sanam Mahoozi
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: Motorists drive past an anti-American billboard in Tehran on Monday. President Trump has threatened Iran with “economic warfare and isolation on an unprecedented scale.”

item.title: Oil Prices Fall Ahead of U.S. Vow to Intensify Economic War Against Iran
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is expected to announce an escalation of sanctions aimed at further isolating Iranian trade.
item.dc:creator: The New York Times
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Reuters

item.title: Farmers Struggle to Get Basic Services From Depleted Agriculture Dept.
item.description: After the departure of thousands of federal workers, rural communities report problems obtaining loans, grants, technical assistance and support for infrastructure and other services.
item.dc:creator: Linda Qiu
item.media:credit: Nina Riggio for The New York Times
item.media:description: Mary and Zachariah Ben turned to private lenders when the low-interest loan they secured from the administration to buy property for their organic baby food business stalled for months.

item.title: In West Texas, Trump’s Border Wall Collides With Latino History
item.description: A century ago, Mexican American families came together to build an adobe church near the border. Can its bell toll again as the wall expansion nears?
item.dc:creator: Jazmine Ulloa and Paul Ratje
item.media:description: The Friends of the Ruidosa Church group has worked to restore the adobe mission for the last 20 years. Members of the group worry that border wall construction could damage the site.

item.title: U.S. Military Kills 2 People in Attack on Boat in Pacific
item.description: The United States has killed at least 223 people since its campaign of boat strikes began nearly a year ago.
item.dc:creator: Eric Schmitt
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:credit: U.S. Southern Command
item.media:description: A screen grab from a video posted by U.S. Southern Command on Monday showed what it said was a vessel operating along a drug-trafficking route in the Eastern Pacific.

item.title: Can Democrats Win Back the Senate? Why Their Chances Are Improving.
item.description: Republicans still have some clear advantages on the map, but President Trump’s unpopularity has opened the door for an outcome that once seemed far-fetched.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk
item.media:credit: Christopher Lee for The New York Times
item.media:description: James Talarico, a Democrat, is trying win a Senate race in Texas after decades of disappointments for his party.

item.title: With Trump Against Him, Can Ralph Norman Win in South Carolina?
item.description: The ultraconservative congressman who has broken with the president on spending is hoping voters reward his experience, contrarian streak and all.
item.dc:creator: Michael Gold
item.media:credit: Will Crooks for The New York Times
item.media:description: Representative Ralph Norman’s recalcitrant posture may have widened the rift that cleared the way for President Trump’s endorsement of Senator Darline Graham.

item.title: Eon Huntley, the Democratic Socialist Running for Office While Working at Bergdorf
item.description: For Eon Huntley, who won his primary in New York in June, good clothes and populist policies go together.
item.dc:creator: Sandra E. Garcia
item.media:credit: James Estrin/The New York Times
item.media:description: Eon Huntley, a 41-year-old candidate for New York State Assembly, has juggled his full-time job at the luxury department store with running a Democratic Socialists of America-endorsed campaign.

item.title: How Should ‘Huckleberry Finn’ Be Taught?
item.description: I traveled around the country to find out if “Adventures of Huckleberry Finn” still has a place in the classroom.
item.dc:creator: Ruth Franklin

item.title: More Companies Are Promising Cloud Seeding Can Make Rain
item.description: States are spending millions of dollars on cloud-seeding technology, backed by new data on its effectiveness — and driven by desperation for water.
item.dc:creator: Scott Dance
item.media:credit: Alex Goodlett for The New York Times
item.media:description: Staff members of Rainmaker, a company based in El Segundo, Calif., that uses drones to seed clouds, prepared for a test flight in southern Idaho last year.

item.title: The Woman Guiding Tourists Through New York City’s Worst Day
item.description: Christina Stanton offers a very specific and deeply personal tour of the World Trade Center site to remind visitors what happened 25 years ago.
item.dc:creator: Michael Wilson
item.media:credit: James Estrin/The New York Times
item.media:description: Christina Stanton leads a North Carolina church youth group on a tour at the 9/11 Memorial reflecting pools. She carries a scrapbook of photos, including those of friends who died on 9/11.

item.title: The Ruthless Efficiency of Ultrapotent Street Drugs
item.description: Five decades after the “war on drugs” sought to make substance abuse unaffordable, illicit drugs are cheaper and more powerful than ever. A visit to Baltimore shows why.
item.dc:creator: Matt Richtel
item.media:credit: KT Kanazawich for The New York Times
item.media:description: Last summer, the city of Baltimore experienced several mass overdose crises, the result of fentanyl being mixed with powerful synthetic chemicals.

item.title: Why Getting High Has Only Gotten Cheaper
item.description: The “war on drugs” sought to reduce substance abuse by driving up prices and lowering demand. Today, street drugs are less expensive and more dangerous than ever.
item.dc:creator: Matt Richtel and Irena Hwang

item.title: Washington Post Ordered to Rehire Fired Columnist Karen Attiah
item.description: An arbitrator ordered the newspaper to reinstate Karen Attiah, who was fired after posting about “white men who espouse hatred and violence” following Charlie Kirk’s killing.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Mullin
item.media:credit: Craig Barritt/Getty Images for Glamour
item.media:description: Karen Attiah in 2018. “This decision confirms what we’ve said from the start: I was doing my job as an opinion writer, and this was wrongful termination,” she said.

item.title: Research Firm’s Founder Explains $6 Million Payment to Fired Forbes Editor
item.description: RJ Shook of Shook Research said he paid Randall Lane, the former top editor at Forbes, for “services and guidance” in partnering with Forbes and later selling his research firm.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Mullin
item.media:credit: Noam Galai/Getty Images
item.media:description: Randall Lane, the former chief content officer of Forbes.

item.title: After Hugging Face Was Attacked By A.I. Agents, It Embarked on a Crusade
item.description: Hugging Face, a start-up that was breached by rogue bots from OpenAI, is using the hack to push for openness in A.I. development.
item.dc:creator: Kate Conger
item.media:credit: Brennan Smart for The New York Times
item.media:description: Clément Delangue, the chief executive of Hugging Face, which is a vocal supporter of open-source artificial intelligence.

item.title: Anatomy of an Autonomous Attack: 5 Alarming A.I. Capabilities
item.description: When OpenAI’s agents went rogue in July, they demonstrated ingenuity and drive beyond what many experts imagined — a dangerous harbinger of what such bots could do in the future.
item.dc:creator: Dylan Freedman
item.media:credit: The New York Times; source photos by Aaron Wojack and Ulysses Ortega for The New York Times

item.title: These Conservatives Want to Be Working Moms. The Manosphere Disapproves.

item.media:description: Interns at the Clare Boothe Luce Center for Conservative Women.

item.title: We’re in a New Era of Class Warfare. History Points to a Way Out.

item.title: Fast-Moving Reno Wildfire Forces Thousands to Evacuate in Nevada
item.description: The Hawk fire has burned more than 15,000 acres since it began on Saturday in the foothills of the Sierra Nevada near Reno.
item.dc:creator: Christina Morales
item.media:credit: Trevor Bexon/Getty Images
item.media:description: The Hawk Fire, has burned more than 15,000 acres and has not been contained since it began on Saturday in the foothills of the Sierra Nevada.
